hunks.summary: The note that ori-runtime >= 2.4.0 implements v2 and does not accept all v1 packages is reflowed beneath the generated Status paragraph, with a blank quoted line; formatting only.

The pointer to skill-hook-isolation/v1 in the header block calls it the contract that will re-enable community hook execution, not the design target, as the status-block wording guard requires. It describes another document and changes no v2 obligation; the body still calls binding executable bytes a design target in that document.

The Tier D provenance paragraph says provenance is the model, a capability grant can never confer Tier D, and Tier D conditions are release-owned under safety-profile/v1, a document this version froze without. New authority statements. Restored out of v2; skills-package/v3 removes Tier D from packages and capability-grant/v1 caps a grant at Tier C.

notes: From runtime f7bd7ebf the loader refuses four things v2 does not state: a manifest member whose value is null, a non-empty condition its rule engine cannot evaluate or longer than 4,096 characters, a Tier D trigger with no condition, and a negative cooldown_seconds. It still upper-cases an ASCII action tier, as v2 shipped. skills-package/v3 states the field-type rules. For Tier D, this version's sentence that a runtime-owned capability grant is the general answer is superseded by skills-package/v3, which removes Tier D from every package, and capability-grant/v1, which caps a grant at Tier C.
